note.text:
Within a family, reactivity changes in a regular way going down the group:
• Alkali metals become MORE reactive down the group: lithium < sodium < potassium. The outer electron is further from the nucleus and is lost more easily. Lithium fizzes gently in water; potassium burns with a lilac flame.
• Halogens become LESS reactive down the group: fluorine > chlorine > bromine > iodine. A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one from its compounds (chlorine + potassium iodide → potassium chloride + iodine).
• Noble gases are unreactive because their outer shell is full.

worked_example.problem: Put {a}, sodium and {b} in order of reactivity with water, most reactive first, and explain.
steps: Reactivity of alkali metals increases down the group.
Down the group the outer electron is further from the nucleus, so it is lost more easily.

cards.idea: Alkali metals get more reactive down the group.
example: Potassium: bursts into a lilac flame.

cards.idea: Halogens get less reactive down the group.
example: Iodine is the least reactive of the four.

cards.idea: A more reactive halogen pushes a less reactive one out of its compound.
example: Chlorine + potassium iodide → potassium chloride + iodine.

pick.q: Chlorine is bubbled into potassium iodide solution. What happens?
pick.r: Iodine is pushed out, because chlorine is more reactive.
w: Nothing, because iodine is more reactive.
e: Chlorine is more reactive than iodine.
Chlorine displaces iodine, not the reverse.
pick.y: A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one.

pick.q: Why is potassium more reactive than sodium?
pick.r: Its outer electron is further from the nucleus, so it is lost more easily.
w: It has a full outer shell.
pick.y: Further from the nucleus, the electron is held less tightly.

pick.q: Why do noble gases not react?
pick.y: A full outer shell is stable.

right.text: Potassium is more reactive than lithium.
Fluorine is more reactive than iodine.
Chlorine displaces iodine from potassium iodide.

wrong.text: Lithium is more reactive than potassium.
wrong.explain: Alkali metals get more reactive down the group: potassium is more reactive.
